chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them:

That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came to the water, and the people of the water came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, these cisterns of ours are visited by beasts, dogs, and livestock. He said:
It has for it what it has taken with its mouths, and for you is the rest of that.

key_terms.السِّبَاعُ: wild beasts that come to drink from the water
key_terms.الْكِلَابُ: dogs that access the water source
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the shared water source being asked about
key_terms.بِأَفْوَاهِهَا: with their mouths, indicating the portion directly taken by the animals
key_terms.حِيَاضَنَا: our cisterns or pools used for storing water
key_terms.سَائِرُ: the remainder, what is left after that

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم rule about water from which animals have drunk?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that when people asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about water frequented by wild animals, dogs, and livestock, he replied that only what the animals took with their mouths belongs to them, while the remainder is for human use. The narration is used in discussions of taharah and the legal status of shared water sources.
